\section*{Chapter 17 - Capability as Proof}


\subsection*{Executive Summary}

\item Capability is not a claim but a maintained proof. Every behavior we rely on has runnable evidence, fresh validation, and a recorded confidence delta.
\item The capability ledger, audits, and problem tracker form a closed loop: add capability -> prove -> monitor -> refresh -> retire.
\item Runnable MCP examples in this chapter let reviewers inspect the live ledger, open issues, and the cognitive audit pipeline that keeps capabilities honest.

\subsection*{Capability Proof Doctrine}

A capability enters the ledger only when all four artifacts are present:

| Requirement | Description | Recorded In |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runnable example | Script, chain, or command that demonstrates the capability end to end. | Chapter example block + \texttt{examples/} | 
| Evidence anchors | SEG nodes with Tier A sources (tests, telemetry, production metrics). | \texttt{evidence.jsonl}, SEG |
| Quartet gate results | Latest SDF-CVF run showing code/docs/tests/tags parity. | Quality dashboards |
| Confidence update | VIF delta after execution; ties confidence to proven reality. | Capability ledger |

Missing any requirement immediately downgrades the capability and blocks dependent work.

\subsection*{Capability Ledger Model}

The ledger is stored in CMC as atoms tagged \texttt{capability}. Each entry captures:

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| \texttt{capability\_id} | Stable identifier referenced by plans and chains. |
| \texttt{description} | Short statement of the behavior proved. |
| \texttt{owner} | Responsible agent or persona (links to specialization profile). |
| \texttt{last\_proved\_at} | Timestamp of most recent successful proof run. |
| \texttt{proof\_artifacts} | Paths to runnable examples, evidence ids, and gate reports. |
| \texttt{vif\_delta} | Confidence change recorded after proof execution. |
| \texttt{status} | \texttt{active}, \texttt{stale}, \texttt{blocked}, or \texttt{retired}. |
| \texttt{next\_audit\_due} | Scheduled audit time based on risk tier. |

Policy files set the audit cadence: Tier S capabilities refresh every 24 hours, Tier A every 72 hours, and Tier B every 7 days.

\subsection*{Validation Lifecycle}

1. \textbf{Register:} APOE chain drafts the capability, links required artifacts, and inserts a pending ledger entry.
2. \textbf{Prove:} Runnable example executes; SDF-CVF gates confirm quartet parity; evidence anchors recorded.
3. \textbf{Assess:} VIF updates confidence; CAS reviews qualitative feedback from collaborators or downstream systems.
4. \textbf{Publish:} Ledger status switches to \texttt{active}; dashboards update and plans referencing the capability unblock.
5. \textbf{Refresh or Retire:} When \texttt{next\_audit\_due} passes or metrics drift, cognitive audits rerun proofs. Failures set status to \texttt{blocked} and open SIS remediation tasks.

\subsection*{Instrumentation and Metrics}

| Metric | Description | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| \texttt{proof\_freshness\_hours} | Hours since the most recent successful proof. | < 72 for Tier A |
| \texttt{audit\_pass\_rate} | Ratio of passed audits in trailing 30 days. | >= 0.95 |
| \texttt{capability\_velocity} | Number of capabilities promoted from pending -> active per week. | Trend tracked |
| \texttt{active\_issue\_count} | Open problems affecting capabilities. | 0 for release |
| \texttt{downgrade\_duration} | Time a capability remains \texttt{blocked} before remediation. | < 12 hours Tier A |

Dashboards in CCS surface these metrics with sparkline trends and links to evidence.

\subsection*{Quartet Parity Validation}

\textbf{Quartet Elements:}
\item \textbf{Code:} Source code files implementing the capability
\item \textbf{Docs:} Documentation describing the capability
\item \textbf{Tests:} Test files validating the capability
\item \textbf{Traces:} Execution traces (VIF witnesses, logs, provenance)

\textbf{Parity Calculation:}
Quartet parity measures semantic alignment across all four elements:
``\texttt{
P = mean(sim(code, docs), sim(code, tests), sim(code, traces),
         sim(docs, tests), sim(docs, traces), sim(tests, traces))
}`\texttt{
Where }sim(x, y)\texttt{ is cosine similarity of embeddings.

\textbf{Parity Thresholds:}
\item Development: P ≥ 0.85
\item Staging: P ≥ 0.90
\item Production: P ≥ 0.95

\textbf{Quintet Parity (Extended):}
Quintet parity adds NL Tags as a 5th element:
}`\texttt{
P\_quintet = mean(P\_quartet, sim(code, tags), sim(docs, tags),
                 sim(tests, tags), sim(traces, tags))
}`\texttt{

\textbf{Gate Enforcement:}
\item Pre-commit: Check quartet completeness and parity before commit
\item CI: Validate quartet parity in pipeline
\item Deployment: Verify quartet parity before deployment
\item Quarantine: Changes with P < 0.90 quarantined

\subsection*{Governance and Escalation}

\item \textbf{Execution blockers:} APOE refuses to execute chains requiring a capability if }status != active\texttt{.
\item \textbf{Confidence routing:} VIF penalizes teams using blocked capabilities; authority for the owning persona decays until proof is restored.
\item \textbf{Override policy:} Temporary overrides require Tier A evidence, explicit justification, and expiry no later than the next audit window.
\item \textbf{Audit trail:} SEG records every promotion, downgrade, override, and remediation step with links to supporting artifacts.

\subsection*{Failure Modes and Responses}

| Failure | Symptom | Response | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Missing proof | Capability lacks runnable example or evidence. | Block execution, open SIS remediation, require new proof before release. | Capability owner |
| Stale proof | }proof\_freshness\_hours\texttt{ exceeds threshold. | Schedule immediate audit; VIF drops confidence; dashboards flag red. | CAS + owner |
| Audit failure | Cognitive audit script errors or gates fail. | Roll back change, run root cause analysis, log resolution in SEG. | APOE operator |
| Synthetic-only proof | Passes mock tests but lacks live data. | Require telemetry anchor; adjust weighting so real-world signals dominate. | Quality lead |
| Duplicate capability | Ledger entries overlap or conflict. | Merge entries, consolidate evidence, reassign ownership. | Capability board |

\subsection*{Integration and Data Flow}

\item \textbf{SDF-CVF:} Supplies quartet parity results; blocks ledger promotions until checks pass.
\item \textbf{CAS:} Tracks capability drift, produces awareness reports, and ensures remediation tasks close.
\item \textbf{SEG:} Stores claims and contradictions; all capability references cite SEG node ids.
\item \textbf{VIF:} Applies confidence updates to related plans, personas, and authority maps (Chapter 19).
\item \textbf{APOE:} Treats capability status as a dependency before scheduling chains; record of proof runs becomes part of execution history.

\subsection*{Capability Proof Architecture}

\subsubsection*{Ledger Storage Architecture}

\textbf{CMC Integration:}
\item Capability ledger stored as CMC atoms tagged }capability\texttt{
\item Each capability entry is an immutable atom with bitemporal tracking
\item Ledger queries use HHNI for hierarchical access
\item SEG links capability claims to supporting evidence

\textbf{Data Model:}
\item \textbf{Atom Structure:} Standard CMC atom with capability-specific fields
\item \textbf{Bitemporal Tracking:} }tx\_time\texttt{ (when recorded) and }valid\_time\texttt{ (when capability was valid)
\item \textbf{Versioning:} Capability updates create new atoms, preserving history
\item \textbf{Indexing:} HHNI indexes capabilities by tier, owner, status for efficient queries

\textbf{Key Insight:} CMC bitemporal storage enables "what capabilities existed at time T?" queries for audit purposes.

\subsubsection*{Proof Execution Architecture}

\textbf{Runnable Example Execution:}
\item Examples stored in }examples/\texttt{ directory with capability\_id references
\item Execution via MCP tools or direct script execution
\item Results captured as VIF witnesses with complete provenance
\item SDF-CVF gates validate quartet parity during execution

\textbf{Execution Flow:}
1. \textbf{Load Example:} Retrieve runnable example from }examples/\texttt{ directory
2. \textbf{Execute:} Run example in isolated environment
3. \textbf{Capture Results:} Store execution results as VIF witnesses
4. \textbf{Validate Parity:} SDF-CVF checks quartet parity
5. \textbf{Update Ledger:} Update capability ledger with proof results

\textbf{Key Insight:} Proof execution architecture ensures capabilities are validated through executable evidence, not claims.

\subsubsection*{Audit Architecture}

\textbf{Automated Audit Pipeline:}
\item Scheduled audits based on tier cadence (Tier S: 24h, Tier A: 72h, Tier B: 7d)
\item CAS monitors capability drift and triggers audits
\item Audit results stored in SEG with evidence anchors
\item Failed audits trigger SIS remediation tasks

\textbf{Audit Process:}
1. \textbf{Trigger:} Scheduled time or drift detection
2. \textbf{Execute Proof:} Run capability proof example
3. \textbf{Validate Parity:} Check quartet parity via SDF-CVF
4. \textbf{Assess Confidence:} Update VIF confidence based on results
5. \textbf{Record Results:} Store audit results in SEG
6. \textbf{Update Status:} Update capability status (active/stale/blocked)

\textbf{Key Insight:} Automated audit architecture ensures capabilities remain proven over time, not just at registration.

\subsubsection*{Case Study: Capability Staleness Detection}

\textbf{Scenario:} Detect and remediate stale capability.

\textbf{Process:}
1. \textbf{Detection:} CAS detects capability }proof\_freshness\_hours\texttt{ exceeds threshold
   - Capability: }mcp\_tool\_retrieve\_memory\texttt{
   - Proof freshness: 96 hours (threshold: 72 hours for Tier A)
   - Status: }active\texttt{ → }stale\texttt{
2. \textbf{Audit Trigger:} Automated audit triggered immediately
   - Audit executes proof example
   - SDF-CVF validates quartet parity (P = 0.88)
   - Parity below threshold (0.90)
3. \textbf{Remediation:} SIS creates remediation task
   - Task: Update quartet elements to restore parity
   - Owner: Capability owner
   - Deadline: 12 hours
4. \textbf{Resolution:} Capability owner updates quartet elements
   - Code updated, docs updated, tests updated, traces updated
   - Parity restored (P = 0.91)
   - Status: }stale\texttt{ → }active\texttt{
5. \textbf{Confidence Update:} VIF updates confidence based on remediation
   - Confidence delta: -0.02 (stale detection penalty)
   - Confidence: 0.88 (from 0.90)

\textbf{Outcome:} Stale capability detected, remediated, and restored to active status with updated confidence.

\textbf{Metrics:}
\item \textbf{Detection Time:} <1 hour (automated)
\item \textbf{Remediation Time:} 8 hours (target: <12 hours) ✅
\item \textbf{Parity Restored:} 0.91 (target: ≥0.90) ✅
\item \textbf{Confidence Impact:} -0.02 (acceptable for remediation)

\textbf{Key Learnings:}
\item Automated staleness detection prevents capability drift
\item Rapid remediation maintains capability quality
\item Confidence updates reflect capability health
\item SIS integration enables systematic remediation

\subsection*{Advanced Capability Scenarios}

\subsubsection*{Scenario 1: Multi-Capability Dependencies}

\textbf{Context:} Capability depends on multiple other capabilities.

\textbf{Challenge:} Ensuring all dependencies are active before capability registration.

\textbf{Solution:}
\item APOE validates all dependencies before capability registration
\item Dependency graph stored in SEG with evidence anchors
\item Failed dependencies block capability registration
\item Dependency status monitored continuously

\textbf{Example:}
\item Capability: }multi\_agent\_coordination\texttt{
\item Dependencies: }mcp\_tool\_send\_ai\_message\texttt{, }mcp\_tool\_get\_ai\_messages\texttt{, }ccs\_coordination\texttt{
\item All dependencies must be }active\texttt{ before registration
\item Dependency graph validated via SEG

\textbf{Key Insight:} Dependency validation ensures capabilities are built on proven foundations.

\subsubsection*{Scenario 2: Capability Versioning}

\textbf{Context:} Capability evolves over time with breaking changes.

\textbf{Challenge:} Maintaining proof for multiple capability versions.

\textbf{Solution:}
\item Each capability version has separate ledger entry
\item Version history tracked via CMC bitemporal storage
\item Proof artifacts versioned alongside capability
\item Deprecated versions marked }retired\texttt{ but preserved for audit

\textbf{Example:}
\item Capability: }mcp\_tool\_store\_memory\texttt{
\item Versions: v1.0 (retired), v2.0 (active)
\item Each version has separate proof artifacts
\item Version history queryable via CMC bitemporal queries

\textbf{Key Insight:} Capability versioning enables evolution while maintaining proof history.

\subsubsection*{Scenario 3: Cross-System Capability Integration}

\textbf{Context:} Capability spans multiple AIM-OS systems.

\textbf{Challenge:} Ensuring proof covers all system integrations.

\textbf{Solution:}
\item Proof artifacts include integration tests
\item SEG links capability to all system integrations
\item Quartet parity validated across all systems
\item Integration failures block capability registration

\textbf{Example:}
\item Capability: }hhni\_retrieval\_with\_vif\_confidence\texttt{
\item Integrations: HHNI (retrieval), VIF (confidence), CMC (storage)
\item Proof includes integration tests for all systems
\item SEG links capability to HHNI, VIF, CMC evidence anchors

\textbf{Key Insight:} Cross-system integration proof ensures capabilities work across system boundaries.

\subsection*{Capability Troubleshooting Guide}

\subsubsection*{Issue: Proof Execution Failure}

\textbf{Symptoms:}
\item Runnable example fails during execution
\item Capability status remains }pending\texttt{ or switches to }blocked\texttt{
\item Audit failures reported

\textbf{Diagnosis:}
1. Check example execution logs
2. Verify quartet elements are present
3. Check SDF-CVF gate results
4. Review VIF witness for errors

\textbf{Resolution:}
1. Fix example execution errors
2. Update quartet elements if needed
3. Re-run proof execution
4. Update capability status

\textbf{Prevention:}
\item Test examples before registration
\item Validate quartet elements before proof
\item Monitor execution logs continuously

\subsubsection*{Issue: Parity Degradation}

\textbf{Symptoms:}
\item Quartet parity drops below threshold
\item Capability status switches to }blocked\texttt{
\item Audit failures due to parity

\textbf{Diagnosis:}
1. Check parity calculation results
2. Identify which quartet elements are misaligned
3. Review recent changes to quartet elements
4. Check SEG for evidence of changes

\textbf{Resolution:}
1. Update misaligned quartet elements
2. Re-run parity calculation
3. Validate parity restoration
4. Update capability status

\textbf{Prevention:}
\item Continuous parity monitoring
\item Pre-commit parity checks
\item Automated parity alerts

\subsubsection*{Issue: Stale Capability Detection}

\textbf{Symptoms:}
\item Capability }proof\_freshness\_hours\texttt{ exceeds threshold
\item Status switches to }stale`
\item Automated audit triggered

\textbf{Diagnosis:}
1. Check last proof execution timestamp
2. Verify audit cadence settings
3. Review capability tier assignment
4. Check for audit execution failures

\textbf{Resolution:}
1. Execute proof immediately
2. Validate proof results
3. Update capability status
4. Adjust audit cadence if needed

\textbf{Prevention:}
\item Automated audit scheduling
\item Staleness monitoring
\item Proactive proof execution
